summary: Read-only cartography of 8 cross-feature interaction domains for the UX/UI GOAL
logs: Mapping 8 interaction domains in parallel (read-only, design-detailed)

current_flows.flow: Auth gate: App.tsx L380 `{user ? <MainTabs/> : <AuthStack/>}`. A guest is a TRUTHY user (AuthContext L370 `isGuest:!isAuthenticated`), so the moment onboarding calls loginAsGuest (OnboardingScreen L256), AuthStack (Language/AuthChoice/Register/Login/Onboarding/PrivacyPolicy) is UNMOUNTED. Any in-app `navigate('AuthChoice'|'Register'|'Login')` from inside MainTabs targets a route that no longer exists.

Cross-tab jumps use nested object form: HomeScreen L453 `navigate('Rappels',{screen:'RemindersMain',params:{screen:'TasksTab',params:{action:'add'}}})` and L484 `navigate('Ressources',{screen:'ResourcesMain',params:{openSearch:true}})`. Most other jumps are bare `navigate('Calendrier')` / `navigate('WeightTracker')` (HomeScreen L443-878).

Notification tap (AppInitializer L447-470): data.screen==='TasksTab' -> `navigate('Rappels',{screen:'TasksTab',...})`; 'Calendar' -> `navigate('Calendrier')`; else `navigate(data.screen,data.params)`.

Web URL deep-link: linking.config (L274-324) maps ~22 routes; getStateFromPath catch-all (L259-273) retries lowercase then falls back to Home. documentTitle formatter (L358-368) maps a 18-entry routeNameToTitleKey, else uses static options.title.

Detail screens entered by deep-link use custom in-body back buttons calling `navigation.goBack()` unconditionally (ArticleDetail L280, SupplementDetail L130, BabyEvolution L156, Statistics L122/134); native header back exists for the rest. No `canGoBack()` guard anywhere in src/.

findings.title: Guest-upgrade dead-end: in-app navigate('AuthChoice') targets an unmounted stack
findings.evidence: AddAppointmentScreen L342 `navigation.navigate('AuthChoice')` and L352 `()=>navigation.navigate('AuthChoice')`; CalendarScreen L380 `navigation.getParent()?.navigate('AuthChoice')`. AuthChoice/Register/Login live ONLY in AuthStack which is unmounted when `user` is truthy (App.tsx L380). A guest is truthy (AuthContext L370 isGuest:!isAuthenticated), so these calls hit a non-existent route -> React Navigation no-ops with a console warning; the guest taps 'Create account' and NOTHING happens. This is the single most common guest-to-paid conversion path and it is silently broken.
findings.proposed_design: Introduce a first-class guest-upgrade flow that works from inside MainTabs. (a) Add a GuestUpgrade route to HomeStack (path 'create-account') that hosts the existing Register UI in 'link mode'. (b) In AuthContext add `upgradeGuest(email,password)` using firebase `linkWithCredential(currentUser, EmailAuthProvider.credential(...))` (the import already exists at AuthContext L630) so guest data is preserved in-place (no re-onboarding). (c) Replace all 3 in-MainTabs `navigate('AuthChoice')` calls with `navigation.navigate('Home',{screen:'GuestUpgrade'})` via getParent for tab-stacks. (d) On success show ToastContext success + pop back to the originating screen so the just-blocked Save/Delete action can be retried. (e) Add a persistent 'Créer un compte' CTA row in ProfileScreen guest badge (L568-577) routing to the same GuestUpgrade screen so the upgrade is discoverable, not only triggered by a blocked write.
findings.files_to_touch: App.tsx (register GuestUpgrade in HomeStack + linking 'create-account'), src/context/AuthContext.tsx (add upgradeGuest via linkWithCredential), src/screens/AddAppointmentScreen.tsx L342/L352, src/screens/CalendarScreen.tsx L380, src/screens/ProfileScreen.tsx L568-577, src/screens/RegisterScreen.tsx (link-mode prop)
findings.acceptance: Guest taps Save appointment -> confirm -> lands on a working Create-account screen inside the tabs (no console warning, no no-op); completing it links the anonymous account, preserves guest data, returns to AddAppointment, and the Save now succeeds. Profile guest badge shows a tappable 'Créer un compte' CTA reaching the same screen.

findings.title: Notification deep-link to TasksTab uses wrong nesting -> opens RemindersTab not Tasks
findings.evidence: AppInitializer L452-456 `navigate('Rappels',{screen:'TasksTab',params:{highlightId}})`. RemindersStack registers ONLY `RemindersMain` (App.tsx L162); TasksTab is a material-top-tab INSIDE RemindersScreen (RemindersScreen.tsx L46). The correct nested path is `Rappels > RemindersMain > TasksTab` (exactly what HomeScreen L453 uses). The notification version skips the RemindersMain level, so React Navigation cannot find 'TasksTab' under the stack -> it lands on RemindersMain's default first tab (RemindersTab), and the highlightId never reaches TasksTab's useFocusEffect (TasksTab.tsx L60-70). User taps a reminder notification and the highlighted task is not shown.
findings.proposed_design: Rewrite the notification branch to mirror the verified HomeScreen nesting: `navigationRef.navigate('Rappels',{screen:'RemindersMain',params:{screen:'TasksTab',params:{highlightId:data.reminderId}}})`. Also gate on `navigationRef.isReady()` (already present L451) and wrap in try/catch like the generic branch (L462-468). Add a one-line comment citing HomeScreen L453 as the canonical shape so the two never diverge again.

Verified by asserting the active material-top-tab is TasksTab and highlightId param is consumed then cleared (TasksTab L70).

findings.title: document.title for detail screens leaks generic label instead of the article/supplement name
findings.evidence: routeNameToTitleKey (App.tsx L334-353) has NO entry for ArticleDetail, SupplementDetail, WeekRecommendations, BabyEvolution, KickCounter, ContractionTimer, HospitalBag, RamadanPregnancy, Diagnostic, LanguageSelect, AddAppointment, TasksTab/RemindersTab. The formatter (L359-366) therefore falls back to `options.title` -> every shared article tab reads 'Article · Mama & Bébé' and every supplement 'Supplément · Mama & Bébé'. A user who opens 5 article links in browser tabs sees 5 identical titles; bookmarks/history are useless and it hurts web SEO/shareability for a content app.

findings.title: Deep-linked detail screen has no safe back target (goBack on empty stack)
findings.evidence: Direct web entry to https://mama-bebe.com/article/:id resolves Home>ArticleDetail as the ONLY route in the Home stack (no HomeMain beneath it). ArticleDetailScreen back button L280 calls `navigation.goBack()` unconditionally; same for SupplementDetail L130, BabyEvolution L156, Statistics L122/134. With an empty back-stack goBack() is a no-op -> the user is stranded on the detail page with a dead chevron and no way to reach Home. No `canGoBack()` guard exists anywhere (grep returned 0).
findings.proposed_design: Create a `useSafeBack()` hook: `const nav=useNavigation(); return ()=> nav.canGoBack() ? nav.goBack() : nav.navigate('Home',{screen:'HomeMain'})`. Wire it into every in-body back button (ArticleDetail, SupplementDetail, BabyEvolution, Statistics) and rely on it for native-header screens via a default headerLeft fallback. This guarantees the chevron always lands somewhere sensible (Home) on cold deep-link entry. Keep the RTL arrow direction logic already present (arrow-forward when isRTL).

findings.title: unmountOnBlur:true silently discards in-tab scroll position and deep stack on every tab switch
findings.evidence: MainTabs L178 `unmountOnBlur:true` (added to fix web multi-H1/leaks). Consequence: switching tabs fully unmounts the previous tab's Stack, so (a) a user reading ArticleDetail in the Home stack, switching to Chatbot and back, is reset to HomeMain losing their place; (b) any list scroll offset (Articles, Reminders) resets to top; (c) half-filled AddAppointment form state is wiped. No scroll-restoration or state-persistence layer exists (grep useScrollToTop/contentOffset found only BabyEvolution's RTL math).
findings.proposed_design: Scope the unmount to the leak it fixes rather than nuking all in-tab state. Option A (preferred): drop `unmountOnBlur:true` and instead fix the original web leak with `detachInactiveScreens` (already set L172) plus `freezeOnBlur:true` (react-native-screens) which stops renders/listeners WITHOUT unmounting, preserving stack + scroll. Option B: keep unmountOnBlur but persist scroll offset per list via a lightweight context keyed by route, restoring on focus through useScrollToTop's inverse. At minimum, guard destructive forms: AddAppointment should warn before its state is dropped on tab blur. Document the chosen trade-off inline since the current comment (L174-178) only justifies unmount, not the UX cost.
findings.files_to_touch: App.tsx L171-209 (tab screenOptions), src/screens/AddAppointmentScreen.tsx (blur-guard), optionally a new src/hooks/useScrollMemory.ts
findings.acceptance: Reading an article, switching to another tab and back, returns to the same article at the same scroll position (or, if Option B, the same list scroll offset). Verify on web no regression to multiple H1 / leaking Firestore listeners that the original unmount fixed.
findings.test_path: (test TO BE CREATED at /Users/1millnonstop/Downloads/pregnancy-app/pre2000/app/e2e/nav-tab-state-retention.spec.ts) — scroll Articles, switch tab, return, assert scrollY preserved; assert single H1 still holds

findings.title: Generic notification deep-link branch can throw on tab-vs-stack route names and lacks fallback
findings.evidence: AppInitializer L462-468 else-branch `navigationRef.navigate(data.screen,data.params)` only catches the throw and logs it. data.screen could be a stack-only route (e.g. 'WeightTracker','ForbiddenFoods','HospitalBag') which lives under the Home tab; a bare top-level navigate to those names works via the global RootParamList augmentation, but unknown/typo screens silently log-and-die leaving the user on whatever screen was open with no feedback. There is also no parity with the web getStateFromPath catch-all (L259-273) which gracefully lands unknown URLs on Home.
findings.proposed_design: Build a single canonical `routeFromNotification(data)` resolver shared by both the notification handler and (conceptually) the linking layer: map known data.screen values to their fully-nested navigate args (TasksTab, Calendar, Home-stack leaves, Chatbot). On an unknown screen, fall back to `navigate('Home',{screen:'HomeMain'})` + a ToastContext info ('Ouverture de l'accueil') instead of a silent catch. This mirrors the web Home fallback (L270) so notification routing and URL routing converge.

findings.acceptance: A notification with an unknown/typo data.screen lands the user on Home (not stuck) with a non-blocking toast; known stack-leaf screens (WeightTracker, HospitalBag) open correctly nested under Home.

findings.title: Cross-tab navigations give no announced feedback and lose focus context for SR/keyboard users
findings.evidence: All cross-tab jumps (HomeScreen L443-878, e.g. `navigate('Calendrier')`, `navigate('Rappels')`) and onStateChange (App.tsx L369-377) only log analytics; no AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility and no programmatic focus move. Centralizing this in onStateChange covers every tab and stack transition uniformly instead of per-screen.

current_flows.flow: LMP/DPA -> pregnancyInfo.week/day: AuthContext.onAuthStateChanged loads userProfiles doc, recomputes currentWeek via calculateCurrentWeek and silently merge-writes it back to Firestore (AuthContext.tsx:172-181). PregnancyContext.load() then re-derives its OWN pregnancyInfo from user.lmp||user.pregnancyStartDate via computeInfo()->calculatePregnancyWeek (PregnancyContext.tsx:83-123,255-257). So week is computed TWICE from the same LMP by two contexts using two different functions, and AuthContext's currentWeek is never read by feature screens.

pregnancyInfo.week -> features: HomeScreen via useCurrentWeek (hooks/useCurrentWeek.ts:18 targetWeek = weekNumber||pregnancyInfo.week||1); HealthDashboard/TasksTab/RemindersTab/WeightTracker/BabyEvolution read pregnancyInfo.week directly. Refresh is per-screen: HealthDashboard refetches on useFocusEffect (HealthDashboardScreen.tsx:138), TasksTab refetches on focus (TasksTab.tsx:62), WeightTracker on focus (WeightTrackerScreen.tsx:97). unmountOnBlur:true means every tab remounts and re-fetches.

week -> month / trimester (NO single source): HomeScreen recomputes trimester inline (HomeScreen.tsx:287); BabyEvolution + BabyGrowthCard derive month via getBabyGrowthForWeek (BabyEvolutionScreen.tsx:47, BabyGrowthCard.tsx:45); RemindersTab reads profile.trimester (RemindersTab.tsx:463) which HomeScreen itself documents as a broken localized ordinal (HomeScreen.tsx:285-288).

baby size cross-surface (two stores): Home hero shows weekData.baby_size_cm from Firestore/local Week docs (HomeScreen.tsx:555); BabyEvolution + BabyGrowthCard show hardcoded monthData.comparison.size strings from babyGrowthData.ts (e.g. month5='14cm', babyGrowthData.ts:117). The two are independent and can disagree for the same week.

guest -> account migration: login()/loginAsGuest() call migrateAllGuestDataToAuth(uid) (AuthContext.tsx:248,430) for tasks/reminders, BUT profile fields (height, prePregnancyWeight) live in guestProfile AsyncStorage and are only merged read-side in PregnancyContext (PregnancyContext.tsx:106-121); they are never written to Firestore on upgrade.

language change -> UI: changeLanguage writes app_locale + i18n.changeLanguage + setupRTL (rtl.ts:78-92); i18n.on('languageChanged') re-syncs document dir (i18n/index.ts:76). Components re-render via useTranslation, but data already loaded into state (week labels, baby_size_label) is not refetched and dir-dependent layout math relying on I18nManager.isRTL stays stale on web.

toast: ToastContext.showToast is the only shared mechanism (ToastContext.tsx:36); used by TasksTab optimistic add/update/error (TasksTab.tsx:107,141,181). HealthDashboard/WeightTracker instead use showAlert for the SAME class of success/error feedback (HealthDashboardScreen.tsx:231,254), so cross-surface feedback is inconsistent.

findings.title: Week is derived twice (AuthContext + PregnancyContext) by two different functions; currentWeek write-back is dead state
findings.evidence: AuthContext.onAuthStateChanged recomputes profile.currentWeek via calculateCurrentWeek(lmpDate) and merge-writes it to Firestore on every cold start (AuthContext.tsx:172-181). PregnancyContext independently recomputes week+day via calculatePregnancyWeek in computeInfo() (PregnancyContext.tsx:255-257). No feature screen reads user.currentWeek — every consumer reads pregnancyInfo.week (useCurrentWeek.ts:18, HealthDashboardScreen.tsx:97, TasksTab.tsx:77, WeightTrackerScreen.tsx:84). The two derivations can momentarily disagree during the load window, and AuthContext's silent setDoc is a wasted write + Firestore-rules surface for a value that is always recomputed on read.
findings.proposed_design: Make pregnancyInfo the single source of truth for derived week. (1) Remove the currentWeek recompute+setDoc from AuthContext.onAuthStateChanged (AuthContext.tsx:172-181) and from login(); treat user.currentWeek as a non-authoritative cache only. (2) Expose a `weekForDisplay` plus a stable `getDerivedPregnancy(lmp)` helper in pregnancyCalculator that returns {week, day, month, trimester, isInvalid} in one call. (3) PregnancyContext.computeInfo calls that one helper and stores {week, dayInWeek, month, trimester, isInvalid, mode} on pregnancyInfo so no consumer recomputes month/trimester locally. Keep AuthContext.currentWeek only for the brief pre-PregnancyContext bootstrap, documented as eventually-consistent.

findings.title: Baby size disagrees cross-surface: Home hero (Firestore baby_size_cm) vs BabyEvolution/BabyGrowthCard (hardcoded babyGrowthData strings)
findings.evidence: Home hero renders `{weekData.baby_size_cm} cm` (HomeScreen.tsx:555) sourced from the per-week Week doc (types/index.ts:13). BabyEvolution renders monthData.comparison.size and BabyGrowthCard the same store, where month 5 (weeks 18-22) is the hardcoded literal '14cm' / sizeInCm:14 (babyGrowthData.ts:115-118). For a user in week 18-22 the hero may show e.g. 14.2 cm while BabyEvolution shows 14 cm for an overlapping week — the documented Mango cross-surface mismatch — because the two stores are independent and month-granular vs week-granular.
findings.proposed_design: Pick the per-week Week doc as the single source for the numeric size and derive the month comparison label/emoji from babyGrowthData (which is the right granularity for the fruit/veg metaphor). (1) In babyGrowthData keep emoji+item label but compute the displayed size from the same Week doc range when available, OR (2) cheaper: add a shared formatBabySize(cm, lang) that rounds consistently (1 decimal) and have BOTH surfaces call it; reconcile month5.sizeInCm to match the midpoint of weeks 18-22 baby_size_cm. Add a build-time consistency test asserting, for each month, |babyGrowthData.sizeInCm - average(Week.baby_size_cm over its weekStart..weekEnd)| <= tolerance.

findings.title: HomeScreen week navigation uses local overrideWeek that never propagates to other surfaces (cross-tab desync)
findings.evidence: HomeScreen keeps overrideWeek/overrideDay in local component state (HomeScreen.tsx:59-60) and passes overrideWeek to useCurrentWeek (HomeScreen.tsx:61). Tapping prev/next sets only that local state (handlePrevWeek/handleNextWeek HomeScreen.tsx:194-215). Because tabs are unmountOnBlur:true, navigating to Calendrier/Rappels and back remounts HomeScreen and resets overrideWeek to null — silently snapping the user from the week they were browsing back to the real current week, with no indication. Meanwhile HealthDashboard/TasksTab keep showing pregnancyInfo.week, so the user can never 'browse week 20 everywhere'.
findings.proposed_design: Decide and unify the contract: week navigation on Home is a *preview* of content, not a global state change. (1) Add a subtle 'viewing week X (not your current week Y)' chip + a one-tap 'back to my week' reset when overrideWeek !== pregnancyInfo.week, so the snap-back on remount is expected and reversible. (2) Persist the last-previewed week in a ref/AsyncStorage ('@home_preview_week') restored on remount so an accidental tab switch does not lose the browsing position. (3) Document that only Home previews weeks; other screens always show the real week. Reset preview automatically when the real week advances (LMP day rollover).

findings.acceptance: Browse to week+2 on Home, switch to Rappels and back: Home still shows week+2 with the 'viewing week X' chip; tapping reset returns to current week; HealthDashboard always shows current week regardless of Home preview.

findings.title: Curious-mode banner shows a frozen exploreWeek snapshot that drifts from the live previewed week each day
findings.evidence: Onboarding curious flow stores a synthetic LMP = today-(exploreWeek-1)*7 (OnboardingScreen.tsx:1166-1168) AND a frozen user.exploreWeek field (AuthContext.tsx:355, types/index.ts:289). PregnancyContext.computeInfo derives the live week from that synthetic LMP (PregnancyContext.tsx:255-257), so the live week advances by 1 every 7 days. But the Home curious banner prints t('home.curiousDesc',{week: user?.exploreWeek || currentWeekNumber}) (HomeScreen.tsx:341), pinned to the original exploreWeek. After a few days the banner says 'exploring week 20' while the rest of Home (hero, baby card) shows week 21+, contradicting itself.
findings.proposed_design: Use a single derived week everywhere in curious mode. Replace HomeScreen.tsx:341 `user?.exploreWeek || currentWeekNumber` with `currentWeekNumber` (the live derived value), OR freeze the WHOLE experience by storing exploreWeek and computing pregnancyInfo from a fixed anchor that does not advance (treat curious as a static snapshot). Recommended: keep it static — in computeInfo, when user.isCurious, set week = user.exploreWeek directly (do not advance from synthetic LMP), so curious users see a stable, consistent week across all surfaces. Drop the dual source.

findings.title: Cross-surface feedback inconsistent: TasksTab uses Toast, HealthDashboard/WeightTracker use blocking showAlert for the same save success/error class

Same shared-state mutation (persist + reload) yields a toast on one screen and a modal alert (or nothing) on another, so users get inconsistent confirmation that their data saved.
findings.proposed_design: Standardize: optimistic mutations that succeed -> showToast(success); recoverable failures -> showToast(error) + revert; only truly blocking/destructive confirmations (delete account, clinical 'save anyway') keep showAlert. (1) In HealthDashboard replace the silent success after persist() with showToast(t('dashboard.saved'),'success') and error showAlert -> showToast where not a clinical gate (HealthDashboardScreen.tsx:251-255,290-295,330-336). (2) Keep showClinicalAlert (HealthDashboardScreen.tsx:192) as-is — it is a deliberate safety gate. Add a tiny useToast call to WeightTracker save success.

findings.title: Guest->account upgrade silently drops physical profile (height/prePregnancyWeight); only tasks/reminders migrate
findings.evidence: On upgrade, migrateAllGuestDataToAuth(uid) runs for tasks/reminders (AuthContext.tsx:248 login, 430 onboarding-signup). Guest physical data (height, prePregnancyWeight) is stored only in the 'guestProfile' AsyncStorage entry and is merged read-side by PregnancyContext (PregnancyContext.tsx:106-121) but never written to Firestore userProfiles on upgrade. loginAsGuest's Firestore write (AuthContext.tsx:381-412) only persists firstName/lmp/dpa/country/TTC fields — not height/prePregnancyWeight. (2) Call it in BOTH the login() (AuthContext.tsx:248) and onboarding-signup (AuthContext.tsx:430) branches. (3) After successful migration, leave guestProfile purge to logout as today. Idempotent + best-effort (never throw).

findings.title: PregnancyContext re-derives week only hourly; daily week rollover at midnight not reflected until an hour later or a profile reload
findings.evidence: computeInfo runs on mount and on a fixed setInterval(...,3600000) 1-hour timer (PregnancyContext.tsx:159-182). useCurrentWeek depends on [pregnancyInfo, ...] (useCurrentWeek.ts:83). A user who crosses a week boundary at midnight while the app is foregrounded keeps the old week for up to an hour (and the hourly tick is wall-clock-arbitrary, not aligned to midnight). There is no AppState 'active' listener to recompute on resume, so backgrounding overnight and resuming also shows a stale week until the next interval fires.
findings.proposed_design: (1) Recompute on app foreground: add an AppState change listener in PregnancyContext that calls computeInfo(profile) when state -> 'active'. (2) Replace the fixed hourly interval with a timer that fires at the next local midnight (compute ms-until-midnight, setTimeout, then re-arm) so the week label flips exactly at day rollover. (3) Keep a cheap hourly safety tick. Guard with the existing profile?.lmp deps.
findings.files_to_touch: app/src/context/PregnancyContext.tsx:159-182
findings.acceptance: With a mocked clock, advancing across local midnight while 'active' updates pregnancyInfo.week within seconds; resuming from background recomputes immediately; no setState-after-unmount warnings (interval/timeout cleared on unmount).
findings.test_path: (test TO BE CREATED at app/src/context/__tests__/PregnancyContext.rollover.test.ts)

findings.evidence: Tabs use unmountOnBlur:true (per nav map) so HomeScreen, HealthDashboard, TasksTab all remount on focus and re-run their fetches: useCurrentWeek re-fetches the Week doc on every mount (useCurrentWeek.ts:27-83, dep targetWeek), HealthDashboard reloads all health collections on focus (HealthDashboardScreen.tsx:138-144), TasksTab reloads weekly+user tasks on focus (TasksTab.tsx:62-74). (2) Optionally lift the current-week Week doc into PregnancyContext (fetch once when pregnancyInfo.week changes, expose weekData) so Home and WeekRecommendations share it. Invalidate cache on logout via clearContentCache (already called, AuthContext.tsx:461).

This is the single shared async-feedback channel for the whole app (used by LanguageSelectScreen.tsx:74 language-updated, AddAppointmentScreen, KickCounterScreen, ContractionTimerScreen, TasksTab, CompletedTasksScreen). A blind/low-vision user gets zero confirmation that their save/delete/language-change succeeded. On web the View is also not focus-managed, and being position:absolute zIndex:9999 it is announced (if at all) out of DOM reading order.

(1) On the Animated.View add accessibilityLiveRegion='polite' (RN/Android) AND accessibilityRole='alert' for iOS VoiceOver; on web RN-Web maps accessibilityLiveRegion -> aria-live, but also explicitly set role='status' aria-live='polite' aria-atomic={true}. (2) For type='error' use accessibilityLiveRegion='assertive' / role='alert' so failures interrupt. (3) Prepend a localized type prefix to the announced string (t('a11y.toastSuccess')/t('a11y.toastError')) so the announcement is self-describing without relying on the emoji (the emoji ✅/❌/ℹ️ should be aria-hidden: add accessibilityElementsHidden + importantForAccessibility='no-hide-descendants' on the icon Text). findings.title: Inconsistent pull-to-refresh: data lists have no refresh affordance, only error-recovery re-fetch
findings.evidence: RefreshControl appears only in HomeScreen, TasksTab, WeightTracker. ArticlesListScreen.tsx:187 (FlatList) and SupplementsListScreen.tsx:170 (FlatList) and WeekRecommendationsScreen (ScrollView) have none — once loaded, the only re-fetch path is hitting the error state's retry. A user who pulls to refresh (universal mobile gesture) gets nothing.
findings.proposed_design: Add a shared useRefresh(loadFn) hook returning {refreshing,onRefresh} and a themed <AppRefreshControl/> wrapper (tintColor=theme.colors.accent, colors=[accent]). Attach to all primary data lists/scrolls: Articles, Supplements, Recommendations, HealthDashboard, Statistics. onRefresh re-runs the same fetch the error-retry uses and shows a success/'updated' toast on completion (or silent). Standardize the spinner color so it is not the default grey/black.

findings.title: No screen-transition language; default platform animation + unmountOnBlur causes abrupt tab swaps
findings.evidence: App.tsx stacks (HomeStack L96, ResourcesStack L125, CalendarStack L140, RemindersStack L157) set only header styling — no `animation`/transition option, so push navigation uses the raw platform default and on web is effectively instant. MainTabs (App.tsx:171-179) sets unmountOnBlur:true, so switching tabs hard-mounts a fresh tree with no crossfade — visible flash, especially with skeleton->content pop.
findings.proposed_design: Define a transition token set in theme.animation (push: slide_from_right native / fade web ~200ms; modal: slide_from_bottom). Apply per-stack screenOptions.animation. For tabs, add a lightweight Animated fade-in (opacity 0->1 over durations.base) on each screen's root container via a shared <ScreenContainer> that also standardizes safe-area + background, gated by useReducedMotion so reduced users get instant. Standardize skeleton->content as a 150ms crossfade rather than an instant swap to reduce the pop.
findings.files_to_touch: app/App.tsx (per-stack animation options), app/src/components/common/ScreenContainer.tsx (new), app/src/theme/index.ts (transition tokens), app/src/screens/ArticlesListScreen.tsx + SupplementsListScreen.tsx (wrap in ScreenContainer / crossfade loaded content)
findings.acceptance: Each stack declares an explicit animation; tab switches fade content in over ~250ms (instant under reduceMotion); skeleton->loaded transition crossfades rather than hard-cuts. No layout shift introduced.
findings.test_path: (test TO BE CREATED at app/src/components/common/__tests__/ScreenContainer.test.tsx) — assert fade animation gated by reduceMotion, renders children; manual web E2E screenshot diff for tab swap

findings.title: OfflineNotice + Toast both anchor to screen edges with no coordination; OfflineNotice is FR-hardcoded fallback and overlaps content
findings.evidence: OfflineNotice.tsx:14-29 is position:absolute top:0 with paddingTop insets.top and default FR strings ('📡 Pas de connexion Internet') as the t() fallback; it overlays the header (no body offset) and there is no spacer so it covers the screen title. Toast (ToastContext.tsx:124-137) is position:absolute bottom — the two feedback layers never reconcile (an offline error toast can stack with the offline banner). OfflineNotice uses raw fontSize 14/12 not typography tokens.
findings.proposed_design: (a) Replace FR string fallbacks with key-only t('offline.title')/t('offline.message') (parity-tested keys in all 4 langs) — never ship French to AR/TN. (b) Add an animated slide-in (translateY -100 -> 0, gated by reduceMotion) and a 1-2px shadow so it reads as an overlay; push body down by reserving its height via a context flag OR make it a non-overlapping inline banner under the header. (c) Use theme.typography.label/caption2 tokens, not raw fontSizes. (d) Suppress 'error'-type toasts about connectivity while OfflineNotice is visible (single offline signal).
findings.files_to_touch: app/src/components/common/OfflineNotice.tsx, app/src/context/ToastContext.tsx, app/src/i18n locale files (offline.title/offline.message x4), app/src/components/common/index.ts (export OfflineNotice)
findings.acceptance: OfflineNotice text comes from locale keys present in all 4 langs (no FR leak on AR/TN), animates in (instant under reduceMotion), uses typography tokens, and does not permanently overlap the screen title. Connectivity error toasts are suppressed while the banner is shown.
